title: Relative output mapping spaces in a cocartesian operadic fibration
statement:
Use quasicategories, mapping spaces and homotopy fibers of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], symmetric infinity-operads and their maps as defined in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping], and colored operator presentations and transport frames of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems]. Work in fixed sufficiently large universes. Let $O$ be a small ordinary symmetric colored operad, allowing nullary operations, and let $B=N(O^\otimes)$ be its operator nerve: an arrow $f:\mathbf c\to\mathbf d$ over $\bar f:\langle n\rangle\to\langle k\rangle$ consists of one operation $\theta_j:(c_i)_{\bar f(i)=j}\to d_j$ for each $1\leq j\leq k$, with no operation for discarded inputs. Let $q:E^\otimes\to B$ be a cocartesian fibration and a map of symmetric infinity-operads. Assume the inert transports give equivalences $E_{\mathbf c}\simeq\prod_i E_{c_i}$, including the empty tuple, where the subscripts denote degreewise fibers over the corresponding tuples. Fix a coherent transport frame and the associated transports $T_\theta$ from the product of input color fibers to the output color fiber.

Every inert edge of $E^\otimes$ is $q$-cocartesian. For $X\in E_{\mathbf c}$ and $Y\in E_{\mathbf d}$ write $x_i,y_j$ for their inert projections. Define $M_f(X,Y)=\operatorname{hofib}_f(\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(\mathbf c,\mathbf d))$. There is an equivalence of spaces, natural in $X,Y$,
$$M_f(X,Y)\simeq\prod_{j=1}^k\operatorname{Map}_{E_{d_j}}\bigl(T_{\theta_j}((x_i)_{\bar f(i)=j}),y_j\bigr).$$
The comparison is the one given by postcomposition with the inert output projections and then factorization through cocartesian transport of the inert input projection followed by the active operation. For $k=0$ the product and $M_f(X,Y)$ are contractible; an empty input block with an output contributes its nullary transport factor, not a deleted factor. No limits or colimits in the color fibers are assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Construction 2.1.1.7, Definition 2.1.1.10(2), Proposition 2.1.2.22 (final assertion), Remark 2.1.2.16, Remark 2.1.3.4; relative fiber and transport formulation of the operadic Segal mapping axiom. Read online; WANTED archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic assertion.

proof.text: Put $S=N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, let $p:B\to S$ be the arity map, and put $r=pq$. These three maps are inner fibrations: for $p,r$ this is part of the symmetric-operad definition in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping]. Suppose $u:U\to V$ has $q(u)$ inert in $B$. For each $Z\in E^\otimes$, stack the precomposition squares for $q$ and $p$, with rows $\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(V,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(U,Z)$, $\operatorname{Map}_B(qV,qZ)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(qU,qZ)$, and the analogous row in $S$. The bottom square is a homotopy pullback by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], since $q(u)$ is $p$-cocartesian. By [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], applied to the transposed diagram, the top square is a homotopy pullback exactly when the outer square is. Applying the mapping criterion again shows that $u$ is $q$-cocartesian exactly when it is $r$-cocartesian. In particular an inert $u$ is $q$-cocartesian, because $q$ preserves inert edges. Conversely any $q$-cocartesian lift of an inert base edge is inert. Thus the frame's actual cocartesian output projections $v_j:Y\to y_j$ are legitimate inert projections for the operadic Segal mapping axiom.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.22, final assertion, printed pp. 183-184; mapping-square proof of the needed special case.

proof.text:
For a pointed map $\alpha$, write $A_E^\alpha(U,V)$ for the inverse image of $\alpha$ in $\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(U,V)$ under the arity map, and similarly write $A_B^\alpha$. These are Kan spaces: apply [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber] to the arity maps, whose mapping-space targets are discrete. Directly from the right-pinched model, a mapping space in the nerve of an ordinary category is the discrete set of its arrows: a functor $[m+1]\to O^\otimes$ constant on the initial face is specified by its last arrow. Postcomposition with $v_j$ and its base projection gives the commutative square with rows
$$A_E^{\bar f}(X,Y)\longrightarrow\prod_j A_E^{\rho_j\bar f}(X,y_j),\qquad A_B^{\bar f}(\mathbf c,\mathbf d)\longrightarrow\prod_j A_B^{\rho_j\bar f}(\mathbf c,d_j).$$
The upper row is the mapping-space Segal equivalence in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping]; the lower row is an isomorphism of discrete sets, since an operator with underlying map $\bar f$ is precisely its list of output operations. Its image of $f$ is $(h_j)_j$, where $h_j=\rho_jf$. Take homotopy fibers at these points. [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] makes the resulting map an equivalence. In the path-space model, a path into a product is exactly a tuple of paths, so the homotopy fiber of this product map is the product of its homotopy fibers. This gives
$$M_f(X,Y)\simeq\prod_j M_{h_j}(X,y_j).$$
Restriction to $A_E^{\bar f}$ does not change the fiber at $f$, since every path in the discrete base is constant.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7 and Definition 2.1.1.10(2), printed pp. 173-174: take the fiber of the two output Segal maps.

proof.text: For each $j$, let $I_j=\{i:\bar f(i)=j\}$ in its induced order and let $\mathbf c_j=(c_i)_{i\in I_j}$. In the ordinary operator category, $h_j$ factors as the inert projection $a_j:\mathbf c\to\mathbf c_j$ followed by the active single-output operator $\theta_j:\mathbf c_j\to d_j$: this follows by writing its one output operation, including when $I_j$ is empty. Let $u_j:X\to X_j$ be the frame's $q$-cocartesian lift of $a_j$. For $i\in I_j$, the composite of $u_j$ with a cocartesian singleton projection of $X_j$ is a cocartesian lift of the singleton projection of $\mathbf c$ by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Compare it with the fixed projection $X\to x_i$ using the same node's equivalence of targets of initial lifts. Hence the Segal coordinates of $X_j$ are coherently the tuple $(x_i)_{i\in I_j}$. Under the frame of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems], transporting $X_j$ along $\theta_j$ therefore has target $Z_j=T_{\theta_j}((x_i)_{i\in I_j})$, with the frame's comparison equivalence understood. The transport lift $b_j:X_j\to Z_j$ and $u_j$ compose coherently to a $q$-cocartesian edge $e_j:X\to Z_j$ over $h_j$, again by the composition assertion. These are the specified inert-then-active lifts, not lifts chosen from a mere existence assertion.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7 and Remark 2.1.2.16, printed pp. 173 and 182: input blocks and their transport functors.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with parameter $K=\Delta^0$, base edge $h_j$, initial object $X$, transport lift $e_j$, and target $y_j$ in the degreewise fiber $E_{d_j}$. Its hypotheses hold since $q$ is an inner fibration with cocartesian lifts; the equivalence between its mapping-square edge condition and our horn condition is [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. The cited transport theorem identifies precomposition with $e_j$ as a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E_{d_j}}(Z_j,y_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{h_j}(X,y_j).$$
Compose the output comparison of step 2 with the inverses of these equivalences. Substituting the expression for $Z_j$ from step 3 gives exactly the asserted product formula. In particular its $j$th component first postcomposes with $v_j$, then factors through $u_j$ followed by $b_j$; it is the comparison specified in the statement, rather than an unspecified equivalence of the two spaces.

source.place: Remark 2.1.2.16, printed p. 182: relative mapping spaces represented by cocartesian transport; the explicit mapping-fiber form is the cited transport theorem.

proof.text: The equivalence is natural in the two fiber objects. The output comparison in step 2 is postcomposition by the coherent inert projections of the fixed frame [def-coef-colored-operator-systems]; varying $X$ precomposes its input and varying $Y$ uses the frame's output transformations. The Segal comparison is therefore a map of these space-valued functors. For step 3, [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] supplies coherent compatibility of successive transports with transport along the composite and with the precomposition maps. Its assertion for every simplicial parameter applies to the frame's diagrams and transformations, so these compatibilities include higher simplices, not only arrows in the homotopy category. Consequently the maps in step 4 are natural equivalences of the same space-valued functors. Inverting such an equivalence and composing with the output map gives a natural equivalence. No objectwise arbitrary inverse is being used: the inverses are inverses of the specified natural equivalences.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4, printed pp. 184-185: pointwise operations in coherent families; use the parametric transport statement for the transport comparisons.

proof.text: When $k=0$, there are no output projections or operations. Both rows in step 2 are equivalences to the one-point empty product; the lower space is literally the singleton consisting of the unique operator to the empty tuple. Its fiber is thus contractible, proving the asserted zero-output case. If $I_j$ is empty but $j$ is an output, $a_j$ projects to the empty tuple, whose degreewise fiber is terminal by the assumed empty Segal equivalence. Transport along $\theta_j:\varnothing\to d_j$ still produces $Z_j=T_{\theta_j}(())$ in the output color fiber. Step 4 retains $\operatorname{Map}_{E_{d_j}}(Z_j,y_j)$; it does not assert this space is contractible or remove it. These arguments also apply when the whole input tuple is empty. All products used here are finite products of spaces or the assumed Segal products; no limit or colimit in a color fiber was required.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2)-(3) and Remark 2.1.2.20, printed pp. 174 and 183: zero arity and the nullary unit operation.
